title: compute/v1 device enrolment (the client's side)
description: What the client (AgentDevice) sends and receives when a person adds their computer: POST /v1/devices, with an enrolment code's credential (made by POST /v1/enrolment-codes with an account key) or, the old path, the person's own login. After enrolment the client joins its owner's NetBird network with the answer's `network` and reports facts with PUT /v1/computers/{id}/facts. README.md "Devices": contracts/compute/v1/README.md.

name.description: The device name the person chose in the client (its default: the computer's own name). An enrolment code made with a `name` decides the name instead.

hostKey.description: The device's SSH host public key in OpenSSH authorized_keys format, generated by the client at its first start and kept. POST /v1/computers/{id}/access answers it as `hostKey`; enrolling again with another key replaces it.

user.description: The OS account the client runs as (on Windows without the computer prefix). Every SSH session runs as this account; /access answers it as `user`.

network.description: How the client's embedded NetBird (client/embed Options) joins the owner's network.

deviceName.description: The peer name to use (embed Options.DeviceName); the computer id, so peers and computers map one to one.

setupKey.description: A one-use NetBird setup key of the owner's account (embed Options.SetupKey). A secret: keep it in memory, never on a command line or in logs.

sshUserCAKeys.description: The SSH user CA's public keys (authorized_keys format, additive 2026-11-11, AgentCompute#179): the computer's own SSH server accepts an OpenSSH user certificate signed by one of them whose one principal is this computer's id (README §3). More than one during a rotation.

deviceKey.description: Only when the enrolment was made with an enrolment code (additive 2026-11-12, AgentCompute#207): the device's own key (key.schema.json scope `device`), answered this once. The client keeps it in a file only its account can read and sends it as its Bearer from then on: it reports this computer's facts, reads the SSH user CA keys and may unbind this computer; it reaches nothing else of the account. It ends when the device is unbound.

codeRequest.description: POST /v1/enrolment-codes: what the code is for. An empty body is the default.

name.description: The name the enrolled computer gets (GET /v1/computers `name`). Without it the client's own name for the computer is used.

ttlSeconds.description: How long the code can be used, from now. Default one hour.

code.description: An enrolment code, as its creation answers it. The code text is answered this once; the service keeps only a SHA-256.

id.description: The code's id: not a secret; logs and errors name it.

code.description: The code the person runs the device client with (`agentdevice join <code>`): one opaque string that holds this service's address and a one-use credential for one POST /v1/devices. A secret until it is used or runs out. Give it to the person; never the account key.
